title: I used Claude, Codex and Suno to build a 3D action horror game in Three.js as a graphic designer with basic HTML/JS knowledge
author: johnreno
selftext:
Hey everyone, first time posting here. Just released Ghost House 3D and wanted to share how the AI side of this actually worked. Also my first time making a 3D game.

It's a fast-paced first-person action game set in a haunted mansion, loosely inspired by the 1986 Sega Master System game Ghost House. I grew up playing the original and always wanted to remake it. The AI workflow is what finally made it possible.

I designed the whole game, art direction, level structure, mechanics and UI. For the AI workflow I used Claude for prompt generation and planning, Codex for implementation and debugging, and Suno to remix the original game soundtrack across multiple genres that transition between room types Banjo Kazooie style. Different areas of the manor have their own feel and the music shifts as you move through them. Really happy with how that part turned out.

On the technical side the trickier stuff was procedural floor generation, frustum culling and distance-based light limiting to keep it running in a browser tab, gamepad support with rumble via the Web Gamepad API, and switching from ACESFilmic to LinearToneMapping because it was crushing the dark areas in gameplay.

The whole thing runs as a single HTML file in the browser. Free to play, Windows and Mac downloads too. Also runs pretty well on Steam Deck via the Linux build.

Would love to know how others manage an AI workflow across multiple tools. Mine was pretty chaotic with multiple terminal windows and build scripts but it got there. Feedback welcome!

[https://johnreno.itch.io/ghost-house-3d](https://johnreno.itch.io/ghost-house-3d)

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: Looking great! I am starting a 3D project here soon and think the stack is really under estimating! I stated of in 2D JS and I have a Asset gen tool you could try using if interested its builds them in either JS or Three.js and is super easy to edit via prompting! free version has character and UI capabilities and you can use pre made asses as well and edit them if formatted the same

replies.author: johnreno
replies.body: Thank you! I’d love to see it, having more control over 3D asset gen sounds great.

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body:
https://trashyio.itch.io/space-game-asset-pack

Its currently only optimized for 2D but have messed around with 3D a bit recently and got pretty good results, treat it like your own custom software and add tools to the UI as needed through prompting. I usually like to do detailed prompt for the first one and describe each body component as its set up to build assets in that way. 

Then edit the asset through a few more prompts and manually tighten anything up. There is currently a bug with gemini so if you don't see the canvas have a preview button, you can copy and paste into a new chat and just say build this exactly. And work through that chat, it is pretty annoying, but still gets the job done as the instructions are baked into the UI layout, so you don't necessarily need to keep it within gemini after the first pass, and am working on getting it packaged into a zip file to used across any LLM. 

Hopefully they get that bug fixed asap as that is the only issue with the workflow I have found. Once you have a polished version built in this format just say let's do a new asset or asset pack in the same art style and similar or matching color palette. Getting that first one done is the only real challenge, but if you already are well versed in three.js I will almost guarantee after a little experimenting. You will get some crazy results!

replies.author: johnreno
replies.body: Thanks, will check it out. It’s amazing what you can do isn’t it? In my game I was trying to solve a problem with 3D models popping up when you got an item, so I asked it to create a 2D voxel version of each model and prebake a rotation (kinda like Fez) and it looked fantastic.

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body: I was going say definitely looks great and am more so curious to see what someone more experienced in the language can do with it! and yeah its pretty insane what you can do with it, AI as a whole that is lol would love to see any results and any feedback if you do decide to mess with it!

comments.author: HallucinatedGames
comments.body: Cool. Curious - Why did you split between Codex and Claude? I’m a heavy Claude Code user, but I also use OpenAI images, etc. What was your experience or thinking or was Amit all vibes! :)

replies.author: johnreno
replies.body: I saw another Reddit post where a combination of both saved credits. Claude Sonnet to generate prompts is cheap and getting Codex to implement was also cheaper. Codex isn’t as smart as Claude but it’s better at implementing into codebases. It seemed to work, I was using way less over a similar amount of work.
